claims.evidence: Witness report shows the TV interface is webOS, but the brand/model text is not clearly readable in the photos.
No photo shows the screen size (inches) or a readable model/label that confirms 86".
Model number is not readable in the witness photos; no label/serial/model plate is shown.
Photos confirm webOS is displayed, but resolution (HD/Full HD/4K) is not shown or measurable from the provided angles.
webOS home screen is visible, but the specific 'AI' features/marketing claims are not verifiable from the photos.

risks.risk: Exact model and screen size may be different from the seller’s words; pricing depends heavily on size/model tier.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the TV’s model/serial label (usually on the back or side) showing the exact model number and screen size.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic LG webOS smart TV with unknown size/model (worst-case tier for value).

risks.risk: Resolution may not be UHD 4K (could be lower), affecting value.
risks.proof: A screenshot from the TV settings showing 'Picture/Resolution' or 'About TV' with the supported resolution (e.g., 4K).
risks.if_unproven: Price as not-confirmed resolution (worst-case: lower than 4K).

risks.risk: Panel defects not visible in the provided angles (dead pixels, lines, backlight bleed, burn-in).
risks.proof: A short video clip showing: solid color screens (red/green/blue/white/black) and a grid test pattern, plus a close-up of any uniform-color areas.
risks.if_unproven: Price as 'possible panel issues' (worst-case: treat as not fully tested).

risks.risk: Ports/inputs may be faulty (HDMI/USB/antenna), which can reduce usability and resale value.
risks.proof: A clip showing HDMI input working (e.g., connect a phone/laptop and display output) and USB playback working.
risks.if_unproven: Price as 'functionality not guaranteed' (worst-case: assume some ports may fail).

risks.risk: Remote control may be missing or not working; affects buyer convenience and value.
risks.proof: Photo of the remote (front/back) and a quick clip showing it navigating the webOS home screen.
risks.if_unproven: Price as 'remote not confirmed' (worst-case: remote missing or untested).

risks.risk: Accessories/wall-mount hardware and stand condition may be incomplete.
risks.proof: Photos showing included items: stand/legs, wall-mount bracket/hardware (if any), power cable, and any manuals/receipts.

risks.risk: External box/set-top box may be included or not; the TV value should not assume it.
risks.proof: Photo/clip showing what exactly is included in the deal (TV only vs TV + external box), with the box model/label visible.
risks.if_unproven: Price as TV only (external box not counted).

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the TV back/side label showing exact model number and serial.
Screenshot from TV 'About/Settings' showing resolution (confirm 4K) and screen size if listed.
Video test: solid color screens + grid pattern to check dead pixels/lines/backlight bleed/burn-in.
Clip demonstrating at least one HDMI input working and one USB playback working.
Photo of the remote control and a short clip proving it navigates webOS.
Photos of included accessories: stand/legs, wall-mount hardware (if any), power cable, and any receipt/warranty.
response.reason: The witness confirms it is a webOS smart TV that is on, but the key details that determine price (exact LG model, confirmed 86-inch size, and confirmed 4K resolution) are not readable or verifiable from the photos. Without those, a worst-case price would be too uncertain.
